newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel lets Palestinians reopen college in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel lets Palestinians reopen college in Hebron.

text.p: Israel allowed Palestinians to partially reopened a college in Hebron on Sunday for the first time since March, Israelis and Palestinians said.

Palestinians arrived for studies at the Polytechnic college in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron after Israeli military authorities allowed officials to open one of its two campuses, witnesses said.

"The army today allowed the opening of two buildings at the Polytechnic college in Hebron as part of a gradual process of opening the institution, conditioned on the preservation of law and order in the area," an Israeli army spokesman said.

Palestinians clashed with Israeli troops last week in Hebron in an attempt to reopen schools closed by Israel after suicide bombings inside Israel by Moslem militants last February and March killed 59 people.
Hebron University, another institution Palestinians want reopened, remained closed on Sunday.
The army spokesman said the decision to reopen the Polytechnic college followed talks between army officers and residents of Hebron, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.
Israel agreed to hand over about 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule under a peace deal signed more than a year ago but its long-overdue partial pullout has yet to take place.
